First, we write the integral as

$$
\int 2{log}_{3}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x=\int 2\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\,\text{d}x=\frac{2}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\int \operatorname{ln}⁡x\cdot 1\cdot \text{d}x.
$$

 

We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x} \\ {v}^{′}=1\, & ⟹\,v=x\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 2{log}_{3}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =\frac{2}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\int \operatorname{ln}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{2}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\int u\,{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{2}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}[uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x] \\  & =\frac{2}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}[x\operatorname{ln}⁡x-\int x\cdot \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x] \\  & =\frac{2}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}[x\operatorname{ln}⁡x-\int 1\,\text{d}x] \\  & =\frac{2x\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}-\frac{2x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}+C \\  & =\frac{2x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}(\operatorname{ln}⁡x-1)+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an integral constant.
